Disney has announced a major milestone coming next month in its plans to merge the Disney+ and Hulu apps, which will be “fully unified” into Disney+ soon.

Disney+ app will fully integrate all Hulu features starting in December

Today Disney reported its quarterly earnings and gave an update on plans to merge Disney+ and Hulu into one app.

Here’s what the company said:

Our app unification of Disney+ and Hulu is nearly complete. Beginning this December, subscribers will have a fully unified experience on Disney+, including live TV and select premium add-ons, creating a more seamless way to discover and engage with the breadth of content across our brands and franchises.

Live TV and premium add-ons were the final Hulu features that hadn’t yet been imported to the Disney+ app. But by adding those capabilities into Disney+, the app unification will be “complete.”

Top comment by Jeremy Martin

The branding is going to get messed up. People look at Disney+ and Hulu as two different unique things. If you make the name just Disney+ people will think what Hulu historically provided is gone.

I find the current integration of Disney+ and Hulu cumbersome. I always find myself going back to my Hulu app to watch content. This may end up being a terrible move for them.

Disney hasn’t said how quickly the Hulu app will be discontinued. But it likely won’t happen until sometime in 2027 at the earliest. The company will want to provide abundant transition time and not risk upsetting its paying subscribers.

The ultimate goal of unifying everything in Disney+, though, will be accomplished soon.

Also in the earnings report, Disney said that creator content will start appearing in the Disney+ app in December. This is related to the company’s deal with TikTok that debuted after its previous OpenAI deal fell apart when Sora was killed off. The Disney+ app will also get “more vertical video, live sports, and podcasts” soon too, Disney said.

What do you think of the plans for the Disney+ app? Let us know in the comments.
